drafted_from: tool:find-silence's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/detect-silence.mjs, and the script run on a synthetic 7 second clip (a tone with silence from 2 to 4 s and from 6 to 7 s)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Find the silent pauses in my talking video and the parts worth keeping." It runs tool:find-silence and hands back the silences and the keep stretches in seconds.
no_lists_because: It reads one video you name by its file identity and answers from that video alone, so it keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find your video's identity in your files: 1f: then 64 hex.

2. Say "Find the silence in this video" with that identity. Optional: threshold_db (quieter than this is silence, default -30), min_silence_seconds (default 0.5), pad_seconds (sound kept around each kept stretch, default 0.05).

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:find-silence. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Read result.silences (start and end) and result.keep (in and out): cut the keep stretches together to remove the pauses.

worked_examples.title: Two pauses found in a 7 second clip
worked_examples.ask: Find the silent parts of my video.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/detect-silence.mjs and run on a 7 second tone clip that is silent from 2 to 4 seconds and from 6 to 7 seconds

worked_examples.title: Only pauses over a second, no padding
worked_examples.ask: Only count pauses longer than a second, keep no extra sound around them.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/detect-silence.mjs, same clip; the 6 to 7 second pause measures 0.975 seconds, under the 1 second minimum, so it is not a silence and its stretch is kept to the end
